# How This Book Is Built {#sec-how-built}

This book is a Quarto book project in the `book/` folder of the workshop repository, built into two
editions from one set of chapter files: an EPUB e-book and a website. It is a worked example of the book's
own subject, and its problems are worth recording, because most of them were invisible until the EPUB was
checked on a phone screen or by a validator.

## One source, two editions {.unnumbered}

The chapters are `.qmd` files. Their Python cells compute every number from the repository's data, by
reading the London files and by importing the water project's `analysis.py`, so the book quotes exactly what
the projects compute. Results are cached with `freeze: auto`, so the EPUB rebuilds quickly and the same way
each time; the rule for clearing the cache, written in the configuration and the README, is to run
`make book-fresh` after any change to the examples' data or analysis.

Content meant for one edition is marked for it. Live 3-D scenes and data explorers are wrapped in
`::: {.content-visible when-format="html:js"}`, and their EPUB stand-ins, animations with a link (and, for the
London map, a QR code), in `when-format="epub"`. The HTML edition runs the workshop's own three.js bundle,
unchanged, through a small script that imitates the slide framework the bundle expects.

## What the EPUB needed {.unnumbered}

Problems met building the EPUB edition, and their fixes:

::: cards
Quarto 1.10.20 drops a book's parts, and the part pages' content, from the EPUB
:   Part pages are ordinary chapters in the EPUB; a post-render script nests each part's
    chapters under it in the table of contents.

A profile's chapter list is added to the base list, not substituted for it
:   One master list (`_chapters.yml`) generates a chapter list for each edition.

`when-format="html"` also matches EPUB
:   HTML-only content uses `when-format="html:js"`.

Rendering one edition empties the other's output folder
:   Each edition has its own output folder.

Quarto's figure wrapper carries an `alt` attribute that EPUB's XHTML forbids
:   The post-render script removes it (the image keeps its alt text).

No landmarks for the copyright page or the start of the text
:   Added by the post-render script, which also puts the copyright page before the preface.

Callout titles and code have fixed light backgrounds and dark text, invisible in a reader's night theme
:   The stylesheet lets the reader's colours through.

Code lines do not wrap on a phone, and cell outputs scroll sideways
:   The stylesheet makes long lines wrap and outputs fit.

Wide diagrams are unreadable on a phone
:   Diagrams are drawn portrait, 700 pixels wide with text of at least 19 pixels, and supplied
    as PNG at double resolution.
:::

The finished EPUB passes EPUBCheck 5.4.0, the W3C's validator, with no errors and no warnings.

## Media {.unnumbered}

All media are rebuilt by one script, `media/build.py`, run by `make media`:

- **Diagrams** are SVG files with a shared style, rasterised to PNG by Chrome. The website uses the SVG, the
  EPUB the PNG, chosen by Quarto's `default-image-extension` for each edition.
- **3-D animations** are recorded from the website edition's live scenes: a script opens the page in Chrome,
  runs the scene's views and drags, captures frames and assembles a GIF with ffmpeg's palette filters.
- **Terminal animations** are recorded with VHS from scripted tapes that run real commands under a demo account,
  so no personal path appears; the agent session is a scripted illustration, because the repository's rules
  rule out paid agent sessions for teaching material.
- **Every GIF opens on its final frame**, held for two seconds, because e-readers that do not animate show a
  GIF's first frame. Each also has a still PNG, which the website shows to readers who ask their system for
  reduced motion. GIFs are kept under 2 MB.
- **The Markdown animations** of @sec-markdown pair what you type, on the left, with what you
  get, on the right. The right-hand side is not drawn: each step on the left was saved in a file
  and rendered by Quarto 1.10.20, and the right shows that page, enlarged. Each opens on its
  finished pair, which is all that a reader without animations shows, then types the source
  from the beginning.

## Reading the EPUB {.unnumbered}

How the EPUB's features behave in different readers:

::: cards
Animated GIFs
:   Readers that animate images play them; others show the first frame, designed as a still.

Night and sepia themes
:   The stylesheet sets no page colours; figures drawn with dark ink sit on a light panel.

Mathematics
:   Written as MathML; readers without MathML support may show it as plain text.

Live 3-D scenes and explorers
:   The website edition only, linked from the EPUB; the London map is also QR-coded.
:::

The repository's `book/README.md` records which readers were tested, and when.

## What was not tested {.unnumbered #sec-not-tested}

Three things the book describes were not tested in full. What was checked, and what was not:

::: cards
The agents' first screens
:   Claude Code's and Codex's first screens were captured on 2026-11-07 (@sec-setup);
    Antigravity's and OpenCode's were not.

The codespace
:   Built from the workshop's dev container and checked on a local computer: Quarto, uv, Git and
    `gh` present, and the first report and the test run render. It was not run on GitHub's own
    machines (@sec-codespace).

The team's workflows
:   The check workflow was run locally with act (0.2.98, in Docker), green on the change and red
    on a broken guard (@sec-team). Pushing, pull requests, the Publish and Monthly reports runs,
    the uv cache and branch protection need a GitHub repository and were not run for this
    edition; their actions and settings were checked against GitHub's documentation on
    2026-11-18.
:::

## Building it {.unnumbered}

From the repository's root folder:

```bash
make book          # both editions, the EPUB post-processing and EPUBCheck
make book-fresh    # the same, re-executing every chapter
make media         # re-record and rebuild every image and animation (slow)
```

`book/README.md` lists the tools each step needs and how to re-record a single animation.
